title: Cauliflower Cheese
subtitle: tender cauliflower in a rich gruyere bechamel
excerpt: Cauliflower cheese is one of the great British comfort dishes. Blanched cauliflower goes into a creamy mustard and cheese sauce, topped with breadcrumbs and more cheese, then baked until bubbling. It works as a side dish with roast meat or as a main with salad.
sourceNotes: Cauliflower cheese has been a staple of British home cooking since the 19th century. Early recipes appear in Victorian cookbooks. It remains one of the most-made vegetable dishes in Britain.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to a day ahead. Bake from chilled, adding 10 minutes to the cooking time.

content.text: Do not overcook the cauliflower. It will cook more in the oven. Aim for just tender when you blanch it -- a knife should meet slight resistance, not slide through.
Preheat the oven to 200C. Blanch the cauliflower florets in boiling salted water for 4 minutes. Drain well and tip into an ovenproof dish.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 2 minutes to form a roux.
Add the milk a little at a time, whisking constantly, until the sauce is smooth and thick.
Remove from heat. Stir in the gruyere, mustard, and nutmeg. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour the sauce over the cauliflower. Mix the breadcrumbs and parmesan and scatter over the top.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and bubbling. Serve hot.

items.fix: Add milk in small additions, whisking thoroughly each time before adding more.
Blanch for only 4 minutes -- it must still have some bite before going in the oven.

content.text: Cauliflower cheese has been part of British cooking since at least the 1700s, when cauliflower first became widely cultivated in Britain. Early recipes use simple cream sauces; the bechamel-based version we know today became standard in the Victorian era. It is served as a Sunday roast side dish, a midweek supper, and a component of the school dinner menu that almost every British child has eaten.
